findings.title: `update` uses organization-wrapped `isEnabled()` when deciding whether to invalidate login caches
findings.body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is fetched via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` when the linked organization is currently disabled. In contrast, the incoming `model` parameter is a plain `IdentityProviderModel` whose `isEnabled()` reflects only the IDP's stored flag. When an enabled login IDP belongs to a disabled organization and is later disabled via `update` (`model.isEnabled() == false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)` evaluates to `false` (because of the disabled organization) and `getLoginPredicate().test(model)` also evaluates to `false` (because the IDP is now disabled). `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then hits the early return at line 405 and skips invalidating the `getForLogin` caches. If the organization was previously enabled when `getForLogin` was cached and is later re-enabled, the now-disabled IDP remains in the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` IDs and will be returned by `getForLogin` even though it is disabled in storage. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())` (unwrapped) should be used for the invalidation comparison, or `getForLogin` callers must also re-check `LoginFilter` / `isEnabled` across all code paths.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias, leaking test IDPs
findings.body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425, copied from line 303), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the string literal `"alias"` rather than the actual IDP alias (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). When the test finishes, cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent IDP named `"alias"` (failing with 404) and leaves the 20 created IDPs in the test realm, which can pollute subsequent tests in the class.

findings.title: `IdentityProviderBean` does not re-check `isEnabled()` on cached `getForLogin` results when `ORGANIZATION` feature is disabled or outside `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`
findings.body: `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` caches the set of internal IDs and resolves each via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, which wraps the model so `isEnabled()` dynamically checks whether the linked organization is enabled. This PR adds `.filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() && ...)` in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (lines 75 and 80) to account for an organization being disabled after `getForLogin` was cached, because disabling an organization does not invalidate `cacheKeyForLogin`. However, `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` itself still returns those disabled-org IDPs in the stream, violating the contract of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` ("An IDP can be used for login if it is enabled..."). Any other caller of `getForLogin` (or `getForLogin` itself) will receive IDPs whose `isEnabled()` is `false`. Filtering by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled` inside `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` (e.g. before returning `identityProviders.stream()`) would enforce the contract for all callers.
